Hi all — adding the technical detail Rishi promised. Below are measured figures from our October run and how the runtime behaves in practice. Please find attached the failover test report and sampled KV warm-cache timings.

Summary (measured medians):
- Warm-cache path (multi-region failover using async replication + pre-warmed nodes): failover completion median = 24 minutes; median KV warm-cache rehydrate = 65 ms per shard (first-request); steady-state tail latencies return within 12 minutes due to lazy rehydration + prefix cache.
- Cold-start path (standby infra boot + disk snapshot restore): full restore median = 2h 35m; RPO observed = 58 minutes (snapshot schedule is every 60m, incremental WAL covers intra-snapshot ops).
- Snapshot cadence: hourly full incremental snapshots; retention 30 days for production customer snapshots, 90 days for Dedicated enterprise with add-on.
- Last full failover test: 2026-10-12 03:10 UTC — test scope: region failover (primary us-west-2 -> standby eu-central-1), owner: SRE runbook team, outcome: successful with identified minor config drift (remediated). See attached PDF (failover-test-2026-10-12.pdf).

Operational notes and caveats:
- For hosted customers, warm-cache SLA is not guaranteed — warm-cache timings vary with workload. We provide guidance and configuration knobs (batching, prefix caching) and can run a workload-specific validation test.
- For Dedicated customers (reserved pools), we can offer improved warm-cache SLAs via configuration and an on-boarding warm-up run; typical committed metric we can support via contract is 1 hour warm-cache to 95th percentile for specified prompt sets.

Attachments: kv-warm-cache-timings.log, failover-test-2026-10-12.pdf

If you want, I can extract a one-page heatmap (SVG/PDF) showing modes and numbers and sign off on the RPO/RTO attestation.
